text: PD-related swallowing impairment can cause aspiration pneumonia, malnutrition and dehydration; assessment and rehabilitation therefore address safety and nutrition as well as symptoms. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-27)

text: Saliva-reducing botulinum toxin can cause dry mouth and dysphagia: these were reported in SIAXI and among the common adverse events in the rimabotulinumtoxinB adult trial. (medium confidence)

text: PD dysarthria can involve reduced volume, monotone pitch, imprecise articulation, altered voice quality and irregular rhythm; it is described as a motor feature even when included in a broader non-motor symptom review. (low confidence)

text: SIAXI randomized 184 adults, including 70.7% with PD, to placebo or incobotulinumtoxinA 75 U or 100 U; the 100 U group improved salivary flow and patient global impression at week 4, with a lasting effect at week 16. These are mixed-population results. (low confidence)

text: NICE recommends speech and language therapy for Parkinson’s disease when communication, swallowing or saliva problems occur; therapy includes swallowing safety strategies such as EMST and effort-based speech strategies. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-27)

text: NICE recommends considering medication for drooling when non-drug management is unavailable or ineffective, considering glycopyrronium bromide and specialist referral for botulinum toxin A. text: SIAXI’s population was 70.7% PD, so its overall results are not PD-only estimates. Treatment-related dry mouth occurred in 5.4% and 2.7%, and dysphagia in 2.7% and 0.0%, of the 75 U and 100 U groups respectively; these findings do not imply swallowing risk is absent. (low confidence)

text: In PD COMM (2024), LSVT LOUD reduced self-reported voice handicap at three months versus no therapy by 8.0 points and versus NHS speech and language therapy by 9.6 points; NHS therapy showed no evidence of benefit over no therapy in this trial. (low confidence)

text: Evidence appraisal differs by level: Troche’s trial reported improved swallowing safety after EMST, whereas Gandhi and Steele’s systematic review characterized intervention evidence as low certainty and found that lower-risk-of-bias studies supported efficiency benefits rather than safety benefits. (medium confidence)

text: In PD COMM, 388 people with PD and dysarthria were randomized. LSVT LOUD used four 50-minute sessions weekly for four weeks plus home practice, and reduced self-reported voice handicap at three months versus no therapy by 8.0 points (99% confidence interval −13.3 to −2.6). (low confidence)

text: PD COMM found no evidence of voice-handicap benefit for the trial’s NHS speech and language therapy arm versus no therapy. It recorded 93 adverse events with LSVT LOUD and 46 with NHS therapy, predominantly vocal strain, with no serious adverse events; the trial was unblinded and used a self-reported primary outcome. (low confidence)

text: The sialorrhea review attributes PD drooling mainly to impaired saliva clearance and reduced swallowing rather than increased saliva production; cited sialometry studies found reduced production relative to people without PD. (low confidence)

text: The SIAXI trial, which included adults with PD and other neurological conditions, found incobotulinumtoxinA 100 U improved salivary flow and patient global change versus placebo at week 4, with effects observed at week 16. NICE supports specialist consideration of botulinum toxin A for drooling. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-27)

text: The dysphagia consensus recommends instrumental assessment to guide treatment; the management review recommends video fluoroscopy or video endoscopy in severe PD to adjust food and liquid consistency. (medium confidence)

text: Short-term swallowing improvements should not be interpreted as establishing comparative or durable superiority of dysphagia therapies: the 2020 systematic review found insufficient evidence to compare techniques, and the 2021 consensus found the treatment literature mainly Class IV. (medium confidence)

text: Dopaminergic medication does not reliably normalize swallowing: the management review states that swallowing does not necessarily improve, while the dysphagia consensus describes antiparkinsonian drug effects as controversial. (medium confidence)

text: Botulinum toxin A and B have treatment evidence for PD drooling: the 2019 MDS review rated both efficacious and clinically useful with specialized monitoring, while SIAXI demonstrated benefit of incobotulinumtoxinA in a mixed neurological population that included PD. (medium confidence)

text: PD COMM recorded 93 adverse events with LSVT LOUD and 46 with NHS speech and language therapy, predominantly vocal strain, with no serious adverse events.
